timelineNote: This file is one snapshot of the Wikipedia settlement markers. The map slider filters verified media. It does not move the line, because an older copy of these markers is not stored here.
summary: Estimated contact line. The map is divided into cells of about 10 km. A cell is counted Russian-held when the nearest Wikipedia settlement marker is Russian-held, and Ukrainian-held when the nearest marker is Ukrainian-held. The line is the boundary between those two kinds of cells. It is drawn solid where that boundary passes within 9 km of a contested marker, or of a close pair of opposing markers with an empty gap between them. Elsewhere it is dashed, because the markers do not pin the boundary down. Where the two markers sit on opposite banks of the Dnipro, the Donets, or the Oskil, the vertex is moved onto that OpenStreetMap river. The tint is the Russian-held cells. Open water near a Russian-held marker can be tinted, because this is not a coastline.
accuracy: Settlement-level estimate, on a grid of about 10 km, not a trench line. Solid stretches are the parts that pass close to a contested marker or a close pair of opposing markers. Dashed stretches are interpolated across a gap in the markers. A village between the markers can sit on either side of a dashed segment. The line is not copied from ISW or DeepStateMap.

Blue dots are treated as Ukrainian-held, red as Russian-held, and the contested mark as contested. Settlements filed under Russia in the module (Kursk, Belgorod, and other Russian cities) are excluded so the international border is not drawn as a front.
